liu_2026_assessment: DOI 10.1038/s41467-026-71808-y resolves (PMID 42009642, PMC13279951, full text read). Zero mentions of Crohn's; patient side is UC only (sc-RNA-seq and biopsies from UC patients on upadacitinib). Cannot set any Crohn's status. It does not contradict Subramanyam 2023: Liu dosed prophylactically (drug from 3 days before DSS; T-cell transfer 'similar effects', supplementary not read) and found tofacitinib non-protective in WT mice even at 450 mg/kg, which matches Subramanyam's prophylactic arm (no prevention at 10 or 40 mg/kg/day); Subramanyam's positive result was the therapeutic (post-onset) arm, which Liu did not test. Together they show the model's tofacitinib readout flips with regimen, which further undermines building a 'model positive, Crohn's negative' contra on it. The upadacitinib-yes/tofacitinib-no pattern matching the Crohn's clinic is the drafter's juxtaposition (rule 5), not the paper's.
missing: safety: cell is empty, yet the class carries Crohn's-trial safety signals (GI perforation in 4 U-EXCEL/U-EXCEED 45-mg patients, herpes zoster; Loftus 2023 PMID 37224198). Whether tox species predicted or were silent on these needs the FDA Xeljanz (NDA 203214) / Rinvoq pharmacology-toxicology reviews; not checked within budget. Likely an untested or contra opener, not a true empty.

dose: Beattie 2017 does derive a model exposure target (colon >=89 ng/g for pSTAT1 inhibition; IC50 1790 ng/g colon, 882 ng/mL plasma) that was never compared with patients. Rule 6 would open the dose strip as untested 2017 rather than leave it empty; judgement call since that work served Theravance's gut-restricted concept, not the class's Crohn's dosing (which came from RA).

Context note: 'DIVERSITY (2025)' for filgotinib not verified within budget; the rest of the note (two tofacitinib phase 2 failures 2014/2017, upadacitinib positive 2023) is confirmed against PMIDs 24480677, 28209624, 37224198.
rule_questions: When the drug class entered a disease with no disease model at all (tofacitinib Crohn's trials 2008-2015 predate every published JAK-inhibitor colitis-model paper; first is Beattie 2017), should the cell carry an untested entry at all, or a distinct 'no model relied on' marker? The brief's 'best model = the one the class relied on' has no model to point at; the draft opens the strip with a later, different sponsor's UC-like model.

Does a later paper that uses the model for the class but makes no patient comparison warrant a second untested entry (status unchanged) just to record that a new model appeared? The brief says one entry per change of status, which argues for merging Subramanyam into entry 1's judgement.

A paper whose only Crohn's content is a background sentence ('efficacious in UC but not CD') while its own comparison is model-vs-UC: the brief's rule 1 says the source must 'make the comparison'. We read that as the source must compare model with THIS context's patients, so this is untested; if the rule only requires any model-patient juxtaposition in the same paper, contra would survive. Worth stating explicitly in the brief.

Minor: file is named jak1-inhibitors but mechanism reads 'JAK inhibitors' and the lead failure (tofacitinib) is pan-JAK; pick one and say whether pan-JAK and JAK1-preferential drugs are one class for this context, since the only clinic-level split (upadacitinib yes, tofacitinib no) runs along that line.
